steps.title: Apply for property tax relief
steps.dek: One form, the PAS-1, covers ANCHOR, Senior Freeze and Stay NJ. Here is the whole process from start to payment.

steps.d: Homeowners and renters can get ANCHOR. Senior Freeze and Stay NJ are for homeowners 65 or older (Senior Freeze also covers people on Social Security disability). Use our benefits checker for a quick read.

• Your 2024 and 2025 property tax bills, or a letter from your tax collector showing taxes paid
  • Your 2024 and 2025 income figures for everyone in the household (Social Security, pensions, IRA withdrawals, interest). Senior Freeze checks both years.
  • Your Social Security number and your spouse's
  • If you rent, your landlord's name and address
File online through the NJ Division of Taxation or mail a paper PAS-1. The deadline is November 2, 2026.
You do not need to send proof of property taxes or income with the PAS-1. The state may contact you later if it needs documents, so keep your tax bills and income records together.

ANCHOR payments start September 15 and Senior Freeze checks began going out July 15. Stay NJ is paid by check, and the state says the 2025 benefit will be paid in February and May 2027. Check your status by calling 1-888-238-1233.

steps.title: Sign up for Medicare at 65
steps.dek: The order of operations for getting Medicare right the first time, including if you're still working.

steps.d: Your Initial Enrollment Period is seven months long. It starts three months before the month you turn 65 and ends three months after. Signing up in the first three months means coverage starts on time.

steps.t: Decide whether you need Part B now
steps.d: If you or your spouse are still working at a company with 20 or more employees and have health coverage through that job, you can often delay Part B without a penalty. Ask your HR office for a written confirmation of coverage.
Apply online at ssa.gov, by phone at 1-800-772-1213, or at a local Social Security office. If you already get Social Security benefits, you'll be enrolled in Parts A and B automatically.
Pick Original Medicare with a Medigap policy and a Part D drug plan, or a Medicare Advantage plan. Read our comparison guide before choosing.
New Jersey's SHIP counselors compare plans for free and sell nothing. Call 1-800-792-8820 for an appointment.
If your income is modest, apply for PAAD, Senior Gold and Medicare Savings Programs. One NJSave application covers several. See Help with prescriptions and bills.

checklists.title: Turning 65 checklist
items: Find your Initial Enrollment Period dates
Ask HR whether your job coverage counts as creditable
Sign up for Medicare Parts A and B (or confirm automatic enrollment)
Compare Medigap + Part D against Medicare Advantage
Book a free SHIP counseling appointment
List every prescription and dose
Confirm your doctors take the plan you choose
Check whether you qualify for PAAD or Senior Gold
Apply for the free NJ State Park Senior Citizen Pass (62+)
Update beneficiaries on retirement accounts

checklists.title: Important papers to keep together
items: Medicare, Medicaid and insurance cards
Social Security award letter
Most recent tax return
Property deed and last two property tax bills
Will and any trust documents
Durable power of attorney
Advance directive or NJ POLST form
List of bank, retirement and investment accounts
List of doctors, medications and pharmacy
Passwords kept in a safe, agreed place

glossary: ADRC
Aging and Disability Resource Connection. New Jersey's network of county offices on aging. Statewide number 1-877-222-3737.
Annual Wellness Visit
A yearly Medicare visit to make or update a prevention plan. It costs nothing if your doctor accepts Medicare.
ANCHOR
Affordable New Jersey Communities for Homeowners and Renters. A yearly property tax benefit for homeowners and renters.
Area Agency on Aging
The county office that plans and funds services for older residents, such as meals, rides and caregiver help.
Assisted living
Housing with help for daily tasks like bathing and medications, but less medical care than a nursing home.
COLA
Cost-of-living adjustment. The yearly raise in Social Security benefits. It is 3.6% for 2027.
Copay
A fixed amount you pay for a covered service or prescription, such as $5 for a generic drug under PAAD.
Creditable coverage
Health or drug coverage at least as good as Medicare's. Having it lets you delay enrolling without a penalty.
Deductible
What you pay each year before your plan starts paying. The 2026 Medicare Part B deductible is $283.
Durable power of attorney
A legal document naming someone to handle your finances if you can't. It stays valid if you lose capacity.
Extra Help
A federal program that lowers Medicare Part D drug costs for people with limited income. Also called the Low Income Subsidy.
Formulary
A plan's list of covered drugs, usually sorted into tiers with different costs.
Initial Enrollment Period
The seven-month window around your 65th birthday when you can first sign up for Medicare.
Inheritance tax
A New Jersey tax on what some heirs receive. Class A heirs, including spouses, children, grandchildren and parents, are exempt.
LIHEAP
Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program. Federal help with heating and cooling bills.
Lifeline
A New Jersey utility benefit of $225 a year for people who qualify for PAAD.
Look-back period
The five years before a Medicaid application when gifts and transfers are reviewed.
Medicaid
Health coverage for people with low income and assets. In New Jersey it is called NJ FamilyCare.
Medicare Advantage
Also called Part C. Private plans that replace Original Medicare, usually with networks and extra benefits.
Medicare Savings Program
State programs that pay Medicare premiums and sometimes copays for people with limited income.
Medigap
Supplement insurance sold by private companies that pays some costs Original Medicare doesn't.
MLTSS
Managed Long Term Services and Supports. NJ FamilyCare's program for long-term care at home or in a facility.
Open enrollment
October 15 to December 7, when anyone on Medicare can change plans for the next year.
Original Medicare
Part A (hospital) and Part B (medical), run by the federal government. You can see any doctor who takes Medicare.
PAAD
Pharmaceutical Assistance to the Aged and Disabled. Cuts prescription copays to $5 or $7.
PACE
Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly. Day center based care that covers medical and support services.
Part D
Medicare prescription drug coverage, sold by private plans.
PAS-1
The single New Jersey application for ANCHOR, Senior Freeze and Stay NJ.
POLST
Practitioner Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment. A medical order, signed with your clinician, that records your wishes.
Respite care
Short-term care that gives a family caregiver a break.
Senior Freeze
New Jersey's Property Tax Reimbursement program, which pays back increases in property taxes for eligible seniors.
Senior Gold
A New Jersey prescription program for people whose income is just above the PAAD limit.
SHIP
State Health Insurance Assistance Program. Free, unbiased Medicare counseling. Call 1-800-792-8820.
Stay NJ
A property tax benefit for homeowners 65 and older that covers up to half of the tax bill, with caps.
Surrogate
The county official in New Jersey who handles probate of wills and estates.
USF
Universal Service Fund. Monthly credits on gas and electric bills for qualifying households.

season.title: Fall foliage drives
season.text: The Delaware Water Gap, Route 23 through High Point and the Skylands roads around Sussex County peak in the second half of October most years.

season.title: Hawk watching at Cape May
season.text: Cape May Point State Park's hawkwatch platform is flat, accessible and busy with migrating raptors every fall.

season.title: Pick your own apples
season.text: Orchards across Hunterdon, Warren and Monmouth counties stay open into late October. Call ahead about wagon rides and walking distances.

season.title: Off-season shore towns
season.text: Ocean Grove, Spring Lake and Cape May are quiet after Labor Day, with easy parking and lower rates.
